title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — roles, params, streaming, tools, response_formatting
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers using OpenAI-compatible endpoints expect /v1/chat.completions parity for role semantics, common params (temperature, top_p, n, stop, max_tokens, logprobs), streaming delta format, and function/tool-calling behavior. This PR implements the compatibility surface for chat.completions while preserving Redwood-native extensions and performance optimizations.

Summary of changes: consolidated request parsing to accept OpenAI-style message arrays (roles: system/user/assistant) and map them to Redwood's internal prompt shape; added support for function/tool calling hooks and the function_response role; implemented `stop` sequence handling with multi-sequence truncation and ensured it interoperates with batching and KV-cache; exposed `logprobs` and `top_logprobs` back to users with approximated per-token scoring when requested; standardized streaming responses to follow OpenAI delta/frame shapes (role transitions, content/piece tokens, function_call events) while keeping our efficient streaming pipeline; added translation layer for legacy Redwood params to maintain backward compatibility and emission of deprecation warnings when appropriate.

Compatibility notes: default behavior remains unchanged for existing Redwood routes; the OpenAI compatibility handler is opt-in via the /v1 prefix or explicit compatibility flag. When users set `stream=true`, we stream OpenAI-style events. `stop` sequences use the same semantics as OpenAI (first-match across sequences, inclusive/exclusive handling documented). `logprobs` returns token-level scores when available; for models/kernels where exact token logprobs are not exposed, we return best-effort approximations and annotate them with a `partial_logprobs` hint in metadata.

Performance/Architecture: Streaming implementation reuses runtime/streaming/streamer.go pipeline; to preserve throughput we added a lightweight event-mapper that transforms internal tokens into OpenAI frames without materializing full responses. Function/tool calling is implemented as a two-stage flow: detect function call in decode, surface function_call info in the final message, and optionally run registered function hooks (user-provided) with the same call signature as OpenAI. Stop handling and logprob calculation were integrated into the token generation loop to avoid extra passes.

Testing and rollout: added unit and integration tests (tests/integration/openai_chat_parity.test) covering role mappings, stop sequences, streaming deltas, and function_call events; added e2e streaming tests that run against the new handler. CI: initial run had a flaky e2e streaming test related to incremental flush timing — fixed by introducing a small jitter and buffer drain window. Canary rollout plan: enable on staging under feature flag, run perf canaries on small and medium models, then enable by default for newly created /v1 routes.

Migration notes for users: - If you use Redwood-native params that overlap (e.g. `redwood.temperature_override`), we keep them but log a single deprecation warning when OpenAI-style params are present. - If you relied on Redwood-specific streaming frames, please switch to OpenAI delta frames or opt out of /v1 compatibility. - Function/tool calling is opt-in and must be registered via the new tools registry; see docs/openai-compat.md for examples.

Files changed (high level): added compatibility layer (api/openai_compat/*), updated streaming pipeline (runtime/streaming/streamer.go), added tests (tests/integration/openai_chat_parity.test) and docs (docs/openai-compat.md), updated Python/TS SDK wrappers to expose compatibility helpers.

Commits (summary): - feat(openai-compat): add request/response mappers for chat.completions - feat(streaming): stream openai delta frames without materializing responses - feat(tooling): function_call detection and hook registry - fix(streaming): flush timing jitter to address e2e flakes - test: add integration/e2e tests and CI workflow

Release notes: Adds OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: message roles, params (temperature, top_p, n, stop, logprobs), streaming delta frames, and function/tool calling. Opt-in via /v1 prefix or feature flag. See docs/openai-compat.md for migration steps.

review_comments: Marcus Li: Overall looks good. Two questions: 1) How do we guarantee stop sequences behave with batching? 2) Can partial logprobs be clearly labeled in responses?

Ava Chen (author): For batching we compute stop checks at token emission time and annotate the batch index; added tests for multi-request batches. Partial logprobs are returned with a metadata flag 'partial_logprobs=true' and documented in openai-compat.md.
Priya Nair: Please add a note about how function_call events are delivered in streaming mode — do we emit a function_call.start event?

Ava Chen: We emit a 'function_call' event when the model decides to call a function; streaming tokens are emitted as normal deltas and the final message contains the 'function_call' object. Added a short doc section and an integration test for this flow.
Ethan Rodriguez: CI failed on first run due to e2e streaming timing; after the fix I re-ran and all checks passed. Approving.
Marcus Li: Approved after tests and minor doc updates.
ci_checks: benchmark: flaky (no regression observed in canary)
release_notes: Adds OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: roles, params (temperature, top_p, n, stop, logprobs), streaming delta frames, and function/tool calling. Opt-in via /v1 prefix or feature flag. See docs/openai-compat.md for details and migration guidance.
notes_for_release_manager: Rollout behind feature flag. Run streaming canaries against small and medium models for 48h. Watch for e2e streaming flush regressions (fixed in this PR but monitor). Notify SDK teams to cut patch releases that expose compatibility helpers.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: mostly additive compatibility layer, but streaming and stop semantics touch the token emission path — thorough canary and alerting required.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover mapping and parameter parsing, integration tests validate streaming deltas and function_call events, e2e tests exercised stop sequences and logprobs. CI initially uncovered a timing flake that was fixed with a drain window and jitter.
